newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian girl killed in amusement park accident.
newsitem.headline: Australian girl killed in amusement park accident.

text.p: Australian police and ambulance services on Sunday said they were investigating the death of a girl killed when part of a ride broke away at an amusement park in a rural area of New South Wales state.
The unnamed 11-year-old girl died and four other children were injured when a carriage on the arm of the "Octopus" ride they were on broke away late on Saturday.
The ride was part of the Rylstone-Kandos Show, an annual rural fair about 200 kilometres northwest of Sydney.
"All five children were taken to Rylstone Hospital, but unfortunately one 11-year-old girl died from massive head injuries," a statement released by the NRMA CareFlight ambulance service said.
The statement also said an 11-year-old boy had suffered "critical" head injuries. He and a 10-year-old boy, also suffering head injuries, were flown overnight to a children's hospital in Sydney.
The condition of both boys had improved on Sunday, CareFlight spokesman Ian Badham told reporters.
Another two children remained in Rylstone Hospital with unspecified injuries.
Three of the children had been in the carriage when it broke off and hurtled into a crowd of onlookers, the CareFlight statement said.
Police from nearby Mudgee said they had worked through the night to determine the cause of the accident.
